bounded_leaf_result.goal_model: After an ambiguous crash around one externally visible effect, recovery must preserve at-most-once effect semantics, avoid omission, and reach a recoverably decidable committed/not-committed state without richer-mode, protected, or manual execution.

minimal_contract.G_generation_scoped_identity: Every logical generation g has one stable durable request identity k(g) bound to the intended payload digest. Retries of the same generation reuse k(g); distinct generations cannot alias; conflicting payload under the same key is rejected.
minimal_contract.I_idempotent_acceptance: Effect acceptance is atomic with respect to k(g): any number of same-generation submissions collapse to at most one externally visible logical effect, and replay returns or preserves the same logical result rather than creating a second effect.
minimal_contract.V_authoritative_generation_visibility: Recovery can authoritatively resolve the state for k(g), correlated to that generation and payload, as committed with result identity or as not committed/pending under semantics that cannot falsely certify completion. The visibility source is authoritative for the externally visible effect, not merely a local checkpoint. Equivalent atomic coupling of effect acceptance with durable generation state satisfies this clause.

necessity_counterexamples.dedupe_without_visibility: Assume G+I but no authoritative V. An attempt may commit and every replay is safely deduplicated, yet all acknowledgments may be lost and the endpoint exposes no committed-state query or authoritative replay result. Recovery can keep retrying without duplication but cannot distinguish committed from not-yet-committed or durably certify outcome completion; any rule that advances can falsely declare an omitted effect, while any rule that never advances violates recoverable progress. Therefore idempotency alone does not supply recoverably decidable completion.
necessity_counterexamples.visibility_without_dedupe: Assume G+V but no I. Original attempt A is in flight when the process crashes. Recovery queries V before A commits and observes not committed, then issues retry B. Without keyed dedupe or an equivalent fence, A and B can both later commit, yielding two visible effects. Thus observation alone does not exclude a delayed original request racing with recovery.
necessity_counterexamples.non_generation_scoped_dedupe: Assume I+V but dedupe identity is reused or can alias across generations g1 and g2. If g1 already committed, a legitimate g2 request with the same key can be suppressed as duplicate, causing omission; if payloads differ, the endpoint may return g1's result for g2 or reject ambiguously. Therefore identity must be generation-scoped and payload-bound, not merely globally reused or coarse-scoped.

bounded_leaf_result.sufficiency_sketch: Under G+I+V, the durable checkpoint stores k(g) before the effect attempt. After any crash, recovery queries V for exactly k(g). If committed, it advances using the authoritative result; if not committed or unresolved, replaying the same k(g) is safe because I prevents a second logical effect, and V eventually provides the authoritative generation-correlated resolution. Cross-generation ABA is excluded by G. This closes the previously identified accept-before-ack crash window at the abstract-contract level.
bounded_leaf_result.equivalence_boundary: A primitive may replace explicit V only if its replay/transaction semantics themselves provide authoritative generation-correlated resolution equivalent to V; a best-effort duplicate response or local repository marker is insufficient.
bounded_leaf_result.exact_missing_capability: One concrete Chat-capable, zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, zero-incremental-cost external-effect primitive satisfying G+I+V (or an equivalent atomic coupling) within the exact target effect class.
